Ensembles of change point models

Source: R/dfr_wwaggr.R
cpd_ensemble.Rd

cpd_ensemble() groups trained change point models (indid() with BCE or InDiD loss, tscp2(), ts2vec(), or calibrated ones) into an ensemble, possibly mixing types; cpd_ensemble_fit() trains the members of an ensemble of one type. The scores of the members (cpd_scores()) are aggregated by wwaggr() or monitored on a stream by dfr_wwaggr().

Usage

cpd_ensemble(members)

cpd_ensemble_fit(
  x,
  labels = NULL,
  model = c("bce", "indid", "tscp2", "ts2vec"),
  n_models = 10,
  boot_sample_size = NULL,
  seed = NULL,
  ...
)

Arguments

members

A list of trained change point models with the same input features.

x

Training sequences, in the formats accepted by indid().

labels

Their labels (0/1 matrix [sequence, time]), for the supervised models.

model

Type of the members: "bce" and "indid" (indid() with that loss), "tscp2" or "ts2vec".

n_models

Number of members.

boot_sample_size

NULL (default): every member is trained on all the sequences and the members differ only by their seeds (the "naive" ensembles of the paper). Otherwise every member is trained on a bootstrap sample of boot_sample_size sequences.

seed

Seed of the ensemble: member i is trained with seed seed + i - 1, and the bootstrap samples are drawn with seed. NULL draws one from the session.

...

Settings of the members, passed to indid(), tscp2() or ts2vec().

Value

A cpd_ensemble object (members).

Details

The paper also compares ensembles trained with stochastic gradient Langevin dynamics; the reference code has no implementation of them and they are not provided.

References

Stepikin, A., Romanenkova, E. and Zaytsev, A. (2025). WWAggr: A window Wasserstein-based aggregation for ensemble change point detection. 2025 IEEE International Conference on Data Mining (ICDM), 1535-1544. doi:10.1109/ICDM65498.2025.00163

Examples

set.seed(1)
make <- function(n) {
  change <- sample(5:24, n, replace = TRUE)
  x <- t(vapply(change, function(c) stats::rnorm(24, ifelse(seq_len(24) < c, 0, 3)), numeric(24)))
  list(x = x, labels = t(vapply(change, function(c) (seq_len(24) >= c) * 1, numeric(24))))
}
train <- make(64)
ensemble <- cpd_ensemble_fit(train$x, train$labels, model = "bce", n_models = 3,
                             epochs = 5, seed = 1)
dim(cpd_scores(ensemble, train$x[1:2, ]))
#> [1]  3  2 24
